Development must comply with landscaping requirements contained in a development control plan that applies to the development.  Specific percentages of open space and landscaped areas are mandated based on building storey count and lot type (infill or freestanding).

Earthworks must not cause a danger to life or property or damage to any adjoining building or structure.  Must not redirect surface or ground water or cause sediment transport to adjoining property. Fill must contain only VENM.
Stormwater must be directed to a public drainage system, an inter-allotment drainage system, or an on-site disposal system.
the works must consist only of— internal alterations to a building
all pipe work is to be located within the building or located underground, with exceptions for proximity to booster connections and building entry points.
height must not exceed 1.5m above ground level and must not cover an area greater than 6m².
works must consist only of internal alterations to a building, or internal alterations plus antenna mounting within specified dimensions.

Before works commence, the applicant must submit to the council a waste management plan that identifies all waste, quantity of waste to be reused, recycled on-site and off-site, and disposed of off-site; specifies how waste will be reused or recycled on-site; and specifies the contractor and waste facility for off-site disposal/recycling.
All new external lighting must comply with AS/NZS 4282:2019 and be mounted, screened and directed to avoid nuisance or light spill.
All driveways and parking areas must be unobstructed.  They must not be used for storage or display of goods, only for vehicular access and parking.
Loading and unloading must not occur on public roads.
Trees and shrubs that fail to establish within 2 years must be replaced. All landscaped areas must be maintained.
Maximum floor space ratio is either the maximum from another instrument or 1:1.
Maximum building height is the greater of the maximum from another instrument or 18m.
New buildings must have a door or window on a facade facing a primary road and a front door or other entrance on the front facade.

Landscaped area must be provided along boundaries adjoining roads, with specific width, soil depth, and planting requirements.  Exemptions exist for alterations/additions to existing buildings that don't increase footprint or decrease landscaped area.
Council or a professional engineer must certify that development on a flood control lot meets specified criteria (9.2).

Development must not increase flooding, meet minimum floor levels, use flood-compatible materials, withstand flood forces, have accessible refuge, and maintain vehicular access above specified flood levels (9.2)
Outside light fittings must be shielded; limits on number of shielded outside light fittings (9.3)
must be located to allow adequate clearance for waste collection vehicles; must not be erected within 5m of residential premises; area must not exceed the greater of 3 car parking spaces or 42m².
containers must be dispatched for reuse or recycling only between 7am-5pm Mon-Sat and 9am-5pm Sun.
may occupy additional car parking spaces if the car park exceeds minimum required spaces, up to 3 additional spaces or 42m².

Development for the purposes of dual occupancies, manor houses, multi dwelling housing, and multi dwelling housing (terraces) must adhere to specified patterns and their associated development standards, location requirements, technical drawings, and technical information.
Development must not be carried out on any part of a flood control lot, other than a part certified as not being a flood storage area, floodway, flow path, high hazard area, or high risk area.
Any part of a building erected is able to withstand flood forces up to the flood planning level (or probable maximum flood level if an on-site refuge is provided).
Development must meet specific standards to mitigate flood risk, including minimum floor levels, flood-resistant materials, and access to refuge areas.
The development must be located within 200m of a public road.
The clauses specify what constitutes 'specified development' under the code and outline the standards that must be met for these developments.

(a) has been certified by a professional engineer, and   
(b) has adequate drainage lines connected to the existing stormwater drainage system for the site, and

Objectives of this section are to conserve environmental heritage, heritage significance of items and areas, archaeological sites, and Aboriginal objects and places.

Development consent is required for demolishing, moving, altering exterior or interior of heritage items, disturbing archaeological sites, disturbing Aboriginal places, erecting buildings on heritage land, subdividing heritage land.
Consent authority MUST notify Heritage Council and consider their response for development on archaeological sites (excluding State Heritage Register sites).
Consent authority MUST consider the effect of development on Aboriginal places of heritage significance.

The objectives of this section are to conserve the environmental heritage of the Western Sydney Employment Area, and to conserve heritage significance of items and areas, including associated fabric, settings and views, archaeological sites, and Aboriginal objects and places.
Councils must conduct advertising design analyses, considering existing and desired character, and the role of outdoor advertising.
